method: Standard five-card poker ranking for one 52-card deck. Every five-card combination of the picked cards (one for five cards, six for six, twenty-one for seven) is scored and the strongest kept, so a seven-card hand reports the best five. A hand is classified as straight flush, four of a kind, full house, flush, straight, three of a kind, two pair, one pair or high card; straights need five consecutive ranks with the ace allowed low as A-2-3-4-5, and a flush needs all five cards in one suit. Ties inside a category are broken by the ranks that make the hand and then by kickers in descending order, which is the usual poker order: pair rank then three kickers; higher pair, lower pair, then kicker; triplet then two kickers; quad then kicker; triplet then pair; and for flushes and high cards all five ranks in order. Suits never rank. Assumes a standard deck with no duplicate cards. Wild cards, jokers, short-deck and lowball variants are not supported, and the tool gives no odds, equity or betting advice.
